messages.author: 238017027312133a
messages.subject: compute quotient of two predictions/parameters
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to fit a spatially-varying coefficient model to some spatiotemporal mortality data I have for counties. I'm specifically interested in fitting this model with race as a covariate and allowing the slope estimates for race to vary spatially and through time. I want to ultimately compute the ratio of deaths in one race category to my "baseline" race category in a given county in a given year and I'm interested in estimating the probability that this ratio is > or < 1.

It seemed like setting up this model in INLA might be the  best way to go about it, but I'm unsure of how to compute the ratios of mortality rates for each county at each time point.

Here's some example code using SIR for cancer in Ohio to set up this model. I'm hoping someone could help me determine the next steps for finding the estimates for mortality ratios. If I were doing this in Stan, I imagine I'd just compute the ratio in the generated quantities block but working with posteriors in INLA is a little more opaque to me right now.

library(INLA)
library(tidyr)
library(spdep)
library(dplyr)
library(sf)
library(SpatialEpi)
library(SpatialEpiApp)

# Import and set up data
namecsv <- "SpatialEpiApp/data/Ohio/dataohiocomplete.csv"
dohio <- read.csv(system.file(namecsv, package = "SpatialEpiApp"))
head(dohio)
nameshp <- system.file(
  "SpatialEpiApp/data/Ohio/fe_2007_39_county/fe_2007_39_county.shp",
  package = "SpatialEpiApp")
map <- read_sf(nameshp)

d <- aggregate(
  x = dohio$y,
  by = list(county = dohio$NAME, year = dohio$year, gender = dohio$gender),
  FUN = sum
)
names(d) <- c("county", "year", 'gender', "Y")

dohio <- dohio[order(
  dohio$county,
  dohio$year,
  dohio$race,
  dohio$gender
), ]


E <- expected(
  population = dohio$n,
  cases = dohio$y,
  n.strata = 2
)
nyears <- length(unique(dohio$year))
countiesE <- rep(unique(dohio$NAME),
                 each = nyears * 2)

ncounties <- length(unique(dohio$NAME))
yearsE <- rep(unique(dohio$year),
              times = ncounties * 2)


dE <- data.frame(gender = c(1, 2), county = countiesE, year = yearsE, E = E)

d <- left_join(d, dE, by = c("county", "year", 'gender'))

d$SIR <- d$Y / d$E


nb <- poly2nb(map)
head(nb)
nb2INLA("map.adj", nb)
g <- inla.read.graph(filename = "map.adj")

d$idarea <- as.numeric(as.factor(d$county))
d$gender <- as.factor(d$gender)
d$idarea2 <- d$idarea1 <- d$idarea
d$idtime <- 1 + d$year - min(d$year)

# Want to model SIR by gender allowing the slopes for gender to vary spatially
# and for the time trend to vary spatially
formula <- Y ~ -1 +
  f(idarea, model = "bym", graph = g, scale.model = TRUE) +
  f(idarea1, gender, model = 'bym', graph = g, scale.model = TRUE) +
  f(idarea2, idtime, model = "bym", graph = g, scale.model = TRUE)

res <- inla(formula,
            family = "poisson", data = d, E = E,
            control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE)
)
summary(res)

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] compute quotient of two predictions/parameters
parts:
Hi

I think you mean that you want the difference between two linear
predictors, since you're with poisson data and using a log-link, so that

risk = exp(lin.predictor)

hence ratios becomes differences.

I made some changes in your code, which you can check out.

since 'gender' (and later 'race') is a factor, it does not make sense to
use a varying regresssion, but its better to say that both genders has
similar response with some correlation (this is 'group=gender' argument;
see the book by Virgilio on www.r-inla.org)

also the bym model (or better the bym2) as buildt-in also an iid random
effect, its better not to use those in this setting.

I guess your example is more of a toy one, and you can follow the same
idea in your real example.

its benefitial to scale the covariates, like time, as you have set the
intercept to 0, otherwise, it does not make sense...

anyway, this is was I guess you want. otherwise let us know

H

parts:
Hello,

Apologies if this message comes through twice. I replied to the initial email, but I think I may have needed to reply in the discussion for it to properly show up. Thank you for your help - it's helped clarify my issue a bit. You are correct, the example I gave you is a toy example. It may not have been the best example to use I'm modeling something slightly different. Let me try and explain again with more mathematical notation to clarify my goals.

I have data on the counts of mortality events in group k in county j in year t, as well as the total population for group k in county j in year t. I have reason to believe that the mortality rates are different in each group k across both time t and space j, so I want to model these differences. The model I think I want is:

log(count_jkt / population_jkt) = alpha_jkt
log(count_jkt) = log(population_jkt) + alpha_jkt

Where log(population_jkt) is the offset and alpha_jkt is the group k intercept in county j at year t and could be decomposed into

log(count_jkt) = log(population_jkt) +  (b_k + u_kj + v_kj + gamma_kt + phi_kt + delta_kjt)

where b_k would be the group k intercept, u_kj is the spatially structured residual for group k in county j modeled with iCAR prior, v_kj would be the unstructured spatial residual for group k in county j, gamma_kt  would be the temporal effect for group k in year t and phi_kt would be a Guassian exchangeable prior for group k in year t. Delta_kjt would be a term to allow the spatial and temporal effects for group k to interact, specifically u_kj and gamma_kt (Type 4 interaction according to the Blangiardo and Cameletti 2015 book, which is what I'm using heavily as a reference, along with this article https://doi.org/10.1080/19475683.2020.1782469).

This model could be rewritten as:
count_jkt / population_jkt = exp(b_k + u_kj + v_kj + gamma_kt + phi_kt + delta_kjt)
If I have k = 3 groups, what I am interested in computing are the ratios of rates in group 2 to group 1 and rates in group 3 to group 1 in each county j and year t:
(count_2jt / population_2jt) / (count_1jt / population_1jt) and (count_3jt / population_3jt) / (count_1jt / population_1jt)

Those ratios should be equivalent to:
exp(b_2 + u_2j + v_2j + gamma_2t + phi_2t + delta_2j) / exp(b_1  + u_1j + v_1j + gamma_1t + phi_1t + delta_1jt)

From those ratios, I want to compute the probability that the ratios are >1 or <1 in each county j at time t.

If I have a variable race that represents my different groups then I think the model formula should look something like this, although I'm not confident it is correct:
formula <- counts ~ offset(log(population)) +
   f(areaID, model = 'bym', graph = g, group = race) +
   f(yearID, model = 'rw', group = race) +
   f(yearID2, model = 'iid', group = race) +
   f(areaID_interaction, model = 'besag', graph = g, group = yearID_interaction, control.group=list(model = 'rw')) 

If you have feedback on correctly specifying this model (or thoughts on if a different modeling approach would be more appropriate) and also how to go about calculating the ratios I described, I would appreciate it.

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] compute quotient of two predictions/parameters
parts:
You can use linear combinations as I described earlier, but I would,
please the offsets in the argument E, so instead of

y ~ offset(log(pop)) + ...

I would use

y ~ ...

with inla(..., E=pop)

then 'pop' does not enter in the linear predictor.

note that in general

Prob( exp(x)/exp(y) > 1) = Prob(exp(x-y) > 1)
= Prob(x-y > 0)

so you do not need the distribution of the ratio, on the difference, to
compute this.

you can also sample fromt the fitted model, see the vignette about this

sample-eval The inla.posterior.sample.eval-function
(source, pdf)


as then its just to return

(Predictor[idx] - Predictor[jdx])

where idx and jdx is the vector of indices for linear predictors you
want to compare, and take the mean



this should really be straight forward.

Best
H
